tasks.short: Troubleshoot robotic systems using actual electronic and mechanical evidence

steps.what: Retrieve the actual robot's fault history, controller revision, wiring diagrams and hydraulic or pneumatic references using native asset filters
inputs: Actual robot identity and existing fault and engineering records
outputs: Verified troubleshooting context and original references

steps.what: Observe the actual robot and capture diagnostic readings from microprocessors, controller, circuits, mechanics, feedback, hydraulics or pneumatics as relevant to the real fault
inputs: Actual robotic system and real diagnostic instruments
outputs: Actual measurements and observed symptoms with component identity

steps.what: Analyse actual circuit, feedback and mechanical evidence, test fault hypotheses and decide the likely fault and unresolved diagnostic questions
inputs: Actual measurements, symptoms and original technical references
outputs: Actual diagnostic finding and remaining uncertainty

steps.what: Write the actual required diagnostic entry identifying observations, readings, reasoning and unresolved faults
inputs: Actual diagnostic work and measurements
outputs: Accurate actual diagnostic entry

steps.what: Save the completed entry in the same robotic service record
inputs: Completed diagnostic entry
outputs: Stored diagnostic entry

tasks.design: Use {OPS_SYSTEM} robot and revision views to retrieve actual history and {DOCS} references. The technician captures real measurements with {OTHER}, the robot diagnostic tools, interprets the fault and writes the actual diagnostic entry.
tasks.previous_blocker: Matching controller revisions and equipment references requires navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native asset and revision filters can reduce that navigation.
tasks.still_hard: Interacting electronic, mechanical and feedback faults require physical evidence and technical reasoning.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a symptom from its cause and recognise inadequate evidence.

ambition.what: Support actual troubleshooting with faster source access.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: asset and revision views can retrieve robotic system references; physical diagnosis remains technical work.

assumptions: Actual prior service authors and engineering owners produce history and diagrams in their existing work; s1 reads and matches them. S2 counts obtaining actual readings, so there is no free structured diagnostic feed. S3 retains hypothesis testing and fault reasoning.

The actual diagnostic record write is separated from physical work in s4. Check native templates first; without demonstrated repetitive fields, no reduction to this small actual entry is claimed. No report after every informal discussion is invented.

No controller load, repair, production movement, external message or return-to-service release is hidden here. Any separately controlled test motion would need its actual readiness and own action represented before expanding this boundary.

Native features already in use have zero new benefit. Same-system save share1 represents negligible time, fully retained and ungated. Shares are unmeasured task-specific effort, not prompt-prior allocations. Where another task maintains this same actual record, a team roll-up must count it once.
unknowns: Are actual controller revisions indexed against the right drawings?
What diagnostic entry is actually required today?
research_questions: Observe source navigation, real reading capture, fault reasoning and actual diagnostic entry separately.

already_counted.description: Actual reference checking, readings, fault reasoning, diagnostic entry and ordinary save remain in s1-s5.

incremental.description: Maintain robot-to-reference links beyond retained diagnostic checks.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High: source navigation15*.20=3 less1 upkeep =2. Low: controller variants are not indexed in the drawing register, so all15 source points require manual tracing and no additional unhelpful view is deployed. Actual measurements45, reasoning30, entry9 and save1 remain fully retained. Unmeasured variant-indexing case.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Install, program or repair controllers, robot tools or conveyors

steps.what: Check actual controller and attached equipment identity, interface requirements, approved logic and existing test and recovery instructions
inputs: Actual controller, tool or conveyor requirements and current engineering instructions
outputs: Verified equipment requirements and permitted change scope

steps.what: Prepare the actual offline controller program for the specified permitted installation change, using a bounded code helper only for explicit logic and checking its meaning against the real equipment requirements
inputs: S1 verified interfaces, explicit permitted logic and actual controller project
outputs: Exact prepared controller program and offline test results

loop.purpose: Draft code expressing explicit permitted controller logic
loop.input: Actual controller project, verified interfaces and explicit requirements
loop.output: Proposed offline code change with requirement mapping
loop.check: Technician checks actual I/O meaning, states, failures and offline test behaviour against original requirements
loop.stop: Reject unsupported interface assumptions or failed checks and code manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Variable code structure needs drafting; existing native blocks and explicit parameter settings are tried first

steps.what: Check actual current isolation, controller state, work permissions and exact prepared program and decide whether the specified installation and load can proceed
inputs: Actual current worksite state and s2 final prepared program
outputs: Current actual operational readiness for the exact identified controller load

steps.what: Install the prepared controller change by loading only the exact program covered by current operational readiness
inputs: Actual controller and exact final program with valid s3 readiness
outputs: Actually loaded controller program and load result

steps.what: Verify the actual controller's loaded version, I/O indications and non-motion diagnostic results and identify remaining defects before any separately authorised movement or production restart
inputs: Actually loaded controller and actual permitted non-motion test checks
outputs: Actual verification results and remaining faults

steps.what: Write the actual required service entry after the controller change and verification, identifying versions, work performed and remaining defects
inputs: Actual completed program load and verification results
outputs: Accurate actual controller service entry

steps.what: Save the completed entry in the same service record
inputs: Completed actual entry
outputs: Stored service entry

tasks.design: Use {OTHER}, the existing controller programming environment, for an offline program draft based on actual verified requirements in {DOCS}. The technician checks semantics and real operational readiness before the separate program-load action, verifies the actual result and writes the required {OPS_SYSTEM} entry.
tasks.previous_blocker: Variable controller code can require repeated composition even after the intended logic is decided.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded code helper can suggest offline code while the actual project, interfaces and tests remain explicit.
tasks.still_hard: Safe logic, real controller state and physical equipment consequences require technical judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise unsupported I/O assumptions and unsafe failure behaviour.

ambition.what: Reduce bounded offline composition within real controller installation work.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: code helpers can draft explicit offline logic but cannot establish controller safety or installation readiness.

assumptions: Representative actual controller-programming installation episode, not a measured mixture of all controller, tool and conveyor repairs. Real engineering owners produce existing requirements; s1 verifies them and s2 counts actual project preparation, code generation, semantic checking and offline tests. No ready-to-load code feed is free.

Try existing controller blocks and configuration first; native runtime already present earns no saving. The loop only assists variable code expression, not requirement selection or operational decisions. All code review remains in s2.

S3 is actual immediate operating readiness within real delegated work authority, not author approval of a written entry. Exact code exists before it; any program, equipment state, isolation or scope change voids a1. Additional real engineering or permit authority is not assumed satisfied. S4 is the one actual controller load; each further load needs its own exact version and current readiness.

No motion, production restart, hardware repair or tool replacement is hidden in the stated non-motion verification. A real broader episode must add those actual actions and gates before estimating it.

Actual service entry is split from the work; ordinary same-system save share1 is negligible, fully retained, ungated and contributes no saving. Actual duplicate service writing across this and service-record tasks must be counted once in a team roll-up. Shares are illustrative and independent of prompt priors.
unknowns: Does the actual controller project support offline checking?
How much variable code is written rather than native parameter configuration?
Which actual operating authority governs the controller load?
research_questions: Observe one actual program revision, count code composition and semantic checking separately and retain all actual load and verification work.

already_counted.description: Verified requirements, retained code production and checking, actual readiness, load, verification and service entry including save remain in s1-s7.

incremental.description: Maintain controller-project access boundaries and helper test examples beyond retained per-change semantic and operational checks.

approvals.approved_version: Exact final offline controller program and configuration produced and tested in s2 for the actual controller under current isolation, equipment state and work scope checked in s3; changes void readiness

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High:25*.20=5 offline program points less2 upkeep=3. Low: controller dialect or undocumented I/O behaviour requires24 of25 programming points, saving only1; do not introduce this helper because its2 upkeep would produce net-1. Keep the existing manual route at zero. Requirements15, readiness10, actual load30, verification15, entry4 and save1 remain fully retained. Unmeasured controller-language and interface constraint.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain service records for robotic equipment and automated production systems

steps.what: Collect actual completed work details, controller or instrument readings and parts information, verify equipment identity and dates and map each actual value into the existing service form
inputs: Actual completed work, real test outputs and parts used
outputs: Verified asset ID, work date, versions, parts, readings with units and source references

steps.what: Populate the unsaved service entry's explicit fixed fields from the actual verified source values using the existing form's mapping or a small deterministic field loader
inputs: S1 verified field values and explicit asset, date, version, parts and measurement mapping
outputs: Proposed unsaved service-entry fields and missing-value exceptions

steps.what: Write the actual service narrative and remaining faults using the existing template and verified source links, retaining technical explanation and uncertainty
inputs: Actual completed service details and proposed fixed fields
outputs: Actual service narrative with verified references

steps.what: Check the complete actual service entry against original work evidence, readings, asset identity, dates, versions and parts and correct missing or misleading content
inputs: Complete proposed service entry and actual original work evidence
outputs: Accurate completed actual service entry

steps.what: Save the completed entry in the same robotic equipment service record
inputs: Checked completed actual service entry
outputs: Stored actual service entry

tasks.design: In {OPS_SYSTEM}, populate the unsaved service form from actual verified fields collected from {OTHER}, the controller and test tools, and use the native narrative template. The technician writes actual explanations and checks the complete record; the ordinary same-system save remains fully retained.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual measured values and service identifiers may be typed repeatedly into record fields.
tasks.enabler_now: Explicit field mapping can prepare the existing form without generating facts or making a maintenance decision.
tasks.still_hard: Source identity, technical explanation and incomplete service evidence require the technician.
tasks.human_edge: Record what actually happened and distinguish a remaining fault from a successful test.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: maintenance forms can populate explicitly mapped identifiers and measurements while source capture and narrative validation remain human work.

assumptions: Conditional on actual observed manual transcription of identifiers and readings into an existing required service record. No new administrative record is invented. Try native form mapping and templates first; mappings already used have no new runtime benefit.

The actual technician performing service produces work details; actual instruments or controller tools produce test outputs. S1 counts collecting, identity checking, unit checking and mapping: asset ID, work date, version, part identity and quantity, measurement value and unit, and source reference. Missing machine-readable values require manual collection in s1 and manual entry instead of s2; there is no free cleaned feed.

S2 prepares draft fields in the same service form; it does not send a report, close an operative work order, authorise equipment use or release a maintenance certificate. S4 is ordinary author checking, not self-approval. S5 is the ordinary same-system save, negligible minimum integer share1, fully retained, ungated and with no saving.

Any actual separate certificate, external report, formal work-order closure or return-to-service commitment must have its real independent final-version authority and distinct gated action; none is smuggled into this save.

Shares are illustrative, not measured or taken from the prompt's prior. If these are the same actual entries already counted in troubleshooting or repair, count that shared record work once when rolling up; do not sum illustrative task episodes as distinct volume.
unknowns: Which actual record fields are still typed manually?
Which controller and test outputs have stable equipment and event identifiers?
research_questions: Observe existing record production and time source collection, repeated field entry, narrative writing and complete checking separately.

already_counted.description: Actual source capture and mapping, retained narrative production, complete record checking and ordinary save remain in s1, s3, s4 and s5.

incremental.description: Maintain controller-output and service-form mappings and inspect mapping failures beyond retained per-entry checking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High:25 fixed-field points plus20*.20=4 reference/template points =29 gross less3 upkeep=26. Low: controller outputs lack stable equipment and event identifiers for most readings, so20 of25 field-entry points stay manual; only5 mapped points plus4 template points save, less3 upkeep=6. Source collection25, complete check29 and save1 remain, and narrative retains16. This is an actual event-metadata availability case, not a shared percentage cut.

steps.what: Read the actual movement requirement, robot and tool frames, limits, payload and current controller program and capture the real target positions and constraints
inputs: Actual robot, movement request, tool and workpiece context
outputs: Verified movement requirement, frame definitions and real target values

steps.what: Modify the actual offline movement sequence, choosing the path, speeds and positions in the native robot programming environment and checking the proposed movement against the real requirement
inputs: Actual verified frames, targets, limits and existing controller program
outputs: Exact proposed movement program and offline check results

steps.what: Check actual current controller state, guarded area, permissions and the exact final movement program before deciding whether its load may proceed
inputs: Exact s2 movement program and actual current worksite and controller state
outputs: Current actual readiness for the specific movement-program load

steps.what: Load the exact permitted modified movement program into the identified robot controller
inputs: Exact final movement program and current s3 operational readiness
outputs: Actual loaded movement-program version and load result

steps.what: After the actual load result, verify the loaded program, real tool and workpiece positions, guarded area and test conditions and decide whether the specified controlled test movement may proceed
inputs: Actual s4 load result and current physical robot and worksite conditions
outputs: Fresh actual readiness decision for the exact controlled test movement

steps.what: Carry out the exact permitted controlled test movement and observe actual path and stopping behaviour
inputs: Actual robot, loaded final movement program and valid fresh s5 readiness
outputs: Actual controlled test movement and observed results

steps.what: Write the actual required movement-change entry with loaded version, observed test results and unresolved conditions
inputs: Actual completed program load and controlled test observations
outputs: Accurate actual movement-change entry

steps.what: Save the completed movement-change entry in the same service record
inputs: Completed actual movement-change entry
outputs: Stored movement-change entry

tasks.design: Keep movement modification in {OTHER}, the existing robot programming and controller environment, using its native frame, path and offline-check tools. Actual program loading and the subsequent controlled physical test each require a separate current operating decision, followed by the real {OPS_SYSTEM} entry.
tasks.previous_blocker: The path must fit the actual tool, workpiece and robot state.
tasks.enabler_now: Native robot programming already supports explicit path editing and offline checks; no additional reduction is established for this episode.
tasks.still_hard: Actual movement and stopping behaviour cannot be inferred from a saved program alone.
tasks.human_edge: Choose the real path and recognise a condition that prevents a safe test.

ambition.what: Retain the actual movement-change process until a specific repetitive operation is observed.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native robot tools support path editing and offline checking, while actual physical movement requires current operating decisions and observation.

assumptions: Before declaring zero, source reading is separated in s1, actual program writing in s2, controller load in s4, actual physical test in s6 and required record writing and saving in s7-s8. Check native parameter, path-template and record-template functions first. The representative episode requires individual path choices; no observed repeated coordinate transcription or templateable entry has been established beyond functionality already used, so no invented saving is claimed.

Actual engineering requirements and real workpiece/tool measurements supply targets; s1 counts their capture, frame and limit checking. S2 counts real path editing and offline checking. No clean trajectory or ready-to-run program feed is assumed.

S3 and s5 are actual current operational readiness decisions within real delegated work authority, not author approval of paperwork. S3 follows the exact final program; s5 follows the actual load result and current physical checks. Changes to program, frames, payload, worksite or conditions void the respective readiness. Any additional real permit or engineering release authority must be represented if required.

Each actual load and physical test action has its own gate; repeated iterations require fresh exact versions and current decisions. No production restart or formal engineering release is hidden in this task episode.

Ordinary same-system save share1 is negligible, fully retained and ungated, with no saving or self-approval. No new system is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero. Shares are illustrative, independent of prompt priors. Deduplicate actual service-entry work across overlapping task episodes in roll-up.
unknowns: Is there actual repetitive coordinate entry that native tools do not already remove?
Which real current operational authorities govern loads and test movements?
